You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-37f0b9db: fill horizontal gaps between markers

## Rule verified on two demonstrations and test
Each row is processed independently. Identify the marker color (5 in the test; examples varied by instance: 5, 6) and the ordinary background (8 in the test; examples: 7, 1). For every pair of consecutive marker cells in the same row, recolor every background cell strictly between them to color 3. Keep the original markers, preserve all cells before the first marker and after the last marker, and leave rows with fewer than two markers unchanged. Do not fill vertical gaps: the successful test output on a 3x27 grid used only rowwise interpolation, and demo outputs provide examples of this same per-row gap filling.

Equivalently, on each row, between the leftmost and rightmost marker, convert background cells to 3, leaving markers as-is. This fills all intervals between markers without extending beyond the outer markers. Preserve any non-background cells if encountered; markers embedded in filled spans remain unchanged.

## Evidence from demo 1
6x28 input, background 7, marker 5. In row 1 (zero-based), markers at columns 2, 14, 23; output filled intervening background cells with 3. Row 2 markers at 8,9,23; output fills cols 10–22 while preserving adjacent 5s. Row 3 has a single marker at col 21 and is unchanged. Other rows show the same behavior with multiple markers; columns after final marker remain background. This supports horizontal interpolation, not full-row filling.

## Evidence from demo 2
22x24 input, background 1, marker 6, fill color 3. Many rows have separated 6 markers; output fills the background between first and last horizontal markers, while preserving all 6s. For example row 2 markers at cols 7,8,17 result in fill at cols 9–16; a row with a sole marker remains unchanged. There are also markers aligned vertically but outputs do not support global vertical interpolation, so apply row-only.

## Test confirmation
3x27, background 8, markers 5. Correct submission filled rows between the first and last marker, keeping the 5s and unchanged leading/trailing backgrounds. Row marker columns: [4,13,18,24], [1,2,8,11,19], [11,20,23]. The accepted output exactly changed background cells within each row's marker span to 3; no vertical gap-fill.

## Practical checks
- Infer marker and background from the current instance; don't hardcode marker 5/background 8.
- Fill color observed as 3 in the samples for this task.
- Keep original marker cells exactly as they are.
- Only fill inside the outer marker span; do not color before first or after last marker.
- Validate every row length and ensure rows with one marker get no fills.
